headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: AutoGPT can write/run commands while slim reads/writes container artifacts and secrets, creating dangerous default interaction paths.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and access the filesystem, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and exposes stdin/stdout plus interactive CLI prompts. If slim outputs untrusted content that AutoGPT ingests from files or terminal transcripts, instruction hijacking is plausible. The pair lacks a documented isolation bridge, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF AutoGPT ingests slim-generated files or terminal output as instructions
IF both agents share a writable workspace or copied transcripts
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable automatic parsing of slim output by AutoGPT
Require manual review before AutoGPT follows file-based instructions
Use read-only mounts for slim outputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress; slim touches certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, and has broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts can flow from slim into AutoGPT and then out through AutoGPT's network path. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF AutoGPT can read files produced by slim
IF slim processes images containing secrets or credentials
mitigations: Keep slim secrets in a separate directory
Block AutoGPT from reading slim output folders
Rotate any registry credentials used by slim
Restrict AutoGPT egress to non-sensitive destinations
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, and AutoGPT can spawn subprocesses while slim can write the filesystem and also spawn subprocesses. If they operate on the same directory, concurrent writes can corrupt artifacts or overwrite each other's outputs. The profiles do not show locking or shared-state protection, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path
IF either agent writes build or analysis outputs without locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one agent at a time on shared paths
Make slim outputs read-only before AutoGPT sees them
Check for file locks before writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate plans or file-based outputs, and slim can act on filesystem artifacts and container targets. If slim treats AutoGPT output as authoritative, a mistaken plan can cascade into destructive container or filesystem actions. Because no verification workflow is documented, the interaction is plausible in default operator workflows but not proven.
conditions: IF slim consumes AutoGPT-produced instructions without human verification
IF AutoGPT writes commands that slim later executes
mitigations: Require human approval before slim executes AutoGPT output
Add a checksum or review step between agents
Limit AutoGPT output to suggestions, not commands
Log and diff all handoffs between agents
requires-engineering: implement structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: slim explicitly handles certificate private keys, environment variables, and registry credentials, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and network egress. If those regulated secrets are placed in a shared workspace, AutoGPT can expose them beyond the intended container boundary. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so compliance risk is inferred from secret handling rather than a named regime.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or credentials are present in slim's target artifacts
IF AutoGPT can access the same files and transmit them externally
mitigations: Exclude secrets from shared paths
Purge credentials from slim inputs before handoff
Restrict AutoGPT to non-sensitive projects
Review retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: separate compliance domains per agent
